rubric.criterion: The agent settles the nine withheld wire constants against the published control figures before computing any figure for the incident window.
The agent records a verdict for every candidate value in a constant's candidate list before selecting that constant's value.
The agent checks the shipped segment and line check totals against the fields they cover before trusting a decoded field.
The agent runs its whole derivation again from the start into a second empty output directory once the constant set is settled.
The agent carries the tick, byte and span arithmetic in Python integers rather than in binary floating point.
The agent edits, deletes or adds files under /app/data during its run.
The agent evaluates its candidate constants against the calibration population's journal rather than against the labelled sample population.
The agent's search leaves exactly one surviving candidate in each of the nine constant lists.
The agent names, for every candidate value it rejects, the published control figure from environment/data/control-slice-figures.json that falsifies it.
The agent settles the blame assignment by iterating over the lock class set until no lock class changes rung between successive passes.
The agent's recovered constants reproduce all eleven published control figures from environment/data/control-slice-figures.json in the trajectory's comparison table.
The response reports a completed calibration pass while the delivered derivation record carries a control figure whose reproduced value differs from its published value.
The agent issues an identical failing command on three or more occasions.
The agent's delivered derive_report.py is written to the ordinary Python practice a reviewer would accept, with names that say what the thing is and errors surfaced rather than swallowed.
